(2) Frozen Foods segment
    At the Research and Development Center of the Ajinomoto Frozen Foods Co., Inc. and the development
    divisions of Group companies overseas, we are developing products that match local tastes and needs.
    Furthermore, through collaboration with the Institute of Food Sciences and Technologies of the
    Company, they are working to provide greater health value, such as salt reduction.

    Frozen Foods (Japan)
    As consumer lifestyles grow more diverse and dining situations change, we have developed lineups
    focusing on meal categories and increased the value provided by frozen foods through efforts such as
    proposing dishes, showcasing dishes in stores, and holding hands-on events.
    In 2024, in Ajinomoto Frozen “GYOZA” series we launched ”Large Pack GYOZA” and we updated our
    “Ginger GYOZA” and “Black Pepper and Garlic GYOZA” products. In all of these products, we use our
    newly improved base for the hane (crispy layer), developed using Ajinomoto Frozen Foods Co., Inc.’s
    unique technologies, to make them less stick to frying pans, similarly to the Ajinomoto Frozen “GYOZA”

                                                    - 65 -
(12 pack) product. We do not use a tray for the “Large Pack GYOZA,” which, therefore, takes little space
in freezers. The new “Ginger GYOZA” has less of the spiciness of ginger than previously, and it contains
no garlic, so people can enjoy as much of it as they want without having to worry about smelling
afterwards. The “Black Pepper and Garlic GYOZA” combines the spiciness of coarsely ground black
pepper with the fragrance of garlic, and behind it all is a hidden ingredient, honey, which gives it an even
richer aftertaste. To heighten the visibility of the AJINOMOTO brand, which is at the heart of our
Gyoza’s brand image, we will update the packaging of our Gyoza and “Microwave GYOZA” to feature
the AJINOMOTO “GYOZA” brand logo. We have designated 2025 as “a year of rebirth for GYOZA,”
and we will further enhance our lineup of products that fit the dining situations and needs of all
consumers and our communications with consumers.
In our “The★” series, which allows people to enjoy restaurant quality at home, we simultaneously
renewed “The★ Shumai,” “The★ Fried Rice,” “The★ Karaage,” and “The★ Hamburg steak.” For “The
★ Shumai,” we improved both the fragrance and texture.
Obento PONTM is a series of dishes for box lunches. They come in tray-less stick packaging, so they can
be easily slipped into open spaces in freezers. They thaw on their own, so they can be put into lunch
boxes as-is, straight from the freezer. The packaging can be rolled up and easily thrown away. This series
of products is drawing attention as a new way to make box lunches. We have released six products in the
“Obento PON” series: “Obento PON” Tsukune, “Obento PON” Karaage, “Obento PON” Tonkatsu,
“Obento PON” Menchi Katsu, “Obento PON” Tori ten, and “Obento PON” Niku dango.
The brand logo for frozen hamburg stake products was unified to the “YoshokuTei Hamburg steak” brand
logo instead of the “YoshokuTei” brand logo. We renewed the < Homemade Demi-Glace Sauce >, adding
mushroom bullion to improve the balance of savory, richness, and bitterness while keeping the hamburg
steak’s bold flavor. We launched “Wakadori Momoyaki,” chicken thigh meat marinated in soy sauce and
crisply grilled over bincho charcoal. We also launched a new frozen karaage product, “Wakadori
Momoyaki” <Lemon salt sauce>, which has a fresh, lemony flavor.
We launched two new frozen fried rice products, Mala Meshi and Pakuchi Meshi. In our frozen toppings
for rice bowls, we launched Mala Mapo tofu don no gu, an appetizing dish with an authentic flavor that is
hard to reproduce at home.

Frozen Foods (overseas)
Due to the increased popularity of Japanese cuisine in North America and Europe, the Asian frozen food
market is growing, especially in the area of retail products. We will continue to use the production
technologies we have refined in Japan to provide easy-to-prepare, delicious products and to constantly
increase the added value of our products, such as by launching products with health functions, as we
further expand our business overseas.
To achieve greater profitability and asset efficiency in our Chinese frozen foods business, we have
reorganized our production system. In 1995, Ajinomoto Frozen Foods Co., Inc., Ajinomoto (China) Co.,
Ltd. (Shanghai), and Life Foods Co., Ltd. (Chuo-ku, Tokyo) established a joint venture, Lianyungang
Ajinomoto Ruyi Foods Co., Ltd. (LAN; Jiangsu Province) to produce packaged chicken products,
packaged vegetable products, and cooked frozen foods for the Japanese market. LAN’s building where
production had been performed grew old, so operations were shut down at the end of April 2024, and
were absorbed and merged in June 2024 into Lianyungang Ajinomoto Frozen Foods Co., Ltd. (AFL;
Jiangsu Province), where the production of fried noodles, primarily for Europe and the US, and sweets,
for Japan and China, was steady, aggregating production activities in AFL.
Furthermore, we also implemented the reorganization of the production system as follows. Ajinomoto
Frozen Foods Co., Inc. and Life Foods Co., Ltd. completed the transfer of all shares of Xiamen
Ajinomoto Life Ideal Foods Co., Ltd. (ALI; Xiamen, Fujian Province), a consolidated subsidiary of
Ajinomoto Frozen Foods Co., Inc., to their joint partner Ruyiqing Group Co., Ltd. (Xiamen, Fujian
Province) in October 2024. A manufacturing license agreement was concluded with ALI, so that ALI
would continue to supply frozen vegetables to Japan and vegetable ingredients to the factories of group
companies (in Japan and China) of Ajinomoto Frozen Foods Co., Inc. for use in their products.

Research and development expenses for the Frozen Foods segment amounted to ¥1,855 million.

(3) Healthcare and Others segment
    We work together with the Research Institute for Bioscience Products & Fine Chemicals, the Institute of
    Food Sciences and Technologies, Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma Services businesses (Belgium, US, Japan,
    India), ZAO “Ajinomoto-Genetika Research Institute” (Russia), Ajinomoto Fine-Techno Co., Inc., and
    other Group companies and their technical development divisions in Japan and overseas, to supply
    products and solutions that contribute to the health and lives of people across the world.

    Amino Acids for Pharmaceuticals and Foods
    To respond to the growth of the market for amino acids for pharmaceuticals and foods, we are continuing
    to develop and introduce fermentation and purification processes with the goals of increasing productivity
    and cost competitiveness. Also, in the culture media business for culturing animal cells, we are using
    Ajinomoto CELLiST Korea Co., Inc. as a platform to continue and expand development in conjunction
    with Japanese and global biopharmaceutical manufacturers.

    Bio-Pharma Services (CDMO Services)
    With regard to contract development and manufacturing of active ingredients for pharmaceutical
    manufacturers, we are striving to enrich our wide-ranging development and supply system for products
    such as small molecule active pharmaceutical ingredients, highly active pharmaceutical ingredients
    (HAPI), peptides and oligonucleotides, protein drugs, and antibody drug conjugates (ADC), and to
    continuously take on orders for new projects.
    In manufacturing of small molecule active pharmaceutical ingredients, we are researching more efficient,
    environmentally friendly processes by fusing our existing technologies with bio-technologies. In our
    contract development and manufacturing of oligonucleotides, we coordinate with GeneDesign, Inc. to
    create a development structure for everything from low volume, high mix production utilizing solid-phase
    synthesis to high volume manufacturing using AJIPHASE® liquid-phase synthesis. While deepening our
    coordination also with S.A. Ajinomoto OmniChem N.V., we are promoting contract development and
    manufacturing of oligonucleotides throughout Ajinomoto’s Bio-Pharma Services (CDMO) business.
    Furthermore, US-based Forge Biologics, Inc., which became a consolidated subsidiary in FY2023, is a
    gene therapy CDMO with strengths in AAV manufacturing and plasmid DNA manufacturing, which are
    key steps in the gene therapy manufacturing value chain. The company has the technology to produce
    high-purity, high-yield AAV vectors. It uses these technologies to produce products in accordance with
    GMP for the clinical trials of numerous biotech companies. By building up a solid manufacturing track
    record, the company has grown and expanded rapidly over the past few years and is expected to continue
    to grow in the future.

    Functional Materials (Electronic Materials and Others)
    Regarding electronic materials, in conjunction with Ajinomoto Fine-Techno Co., Inc., we are developing
    Ajinomoto Build-up Film® (ABF) for next-generation personal computers, data center servers, and 5G
    communications networks.

    Others
    —Functional nutritional foods—
    aminoVITAL® is a sports supplement brand launched in 1995 that applies the findings of
    “AminoScience,” which we have been developing for over a century, to the sports field. It has primarily
    enjoyed the support of top athletes and people who train hard. We also wanted to contribute to the mental
    and physical health of even more consumers through exercise, and on the 30th anniversary of the brand,
    we launched aminoVITAL® amiKatsu, a jelly drink that can be easily enjoyed in day-to-day life, such as
    an additional breakfast item or as a snack. It contains amino acids (3,000 mg) such as alanine, proline,
    BCAA, and arginine as energy sources, and not only can it be used for providing nutrients that often go
    lacking, such as vitamins or dietary fiber, but it was also developed using the Ajinomoto Group’s unique
    target quality design technology, AJI-PMap® to select the functional characteristics best suited for
    mornings, when jelly drinks are most often used. It reproduces the distinctive texture and flavor of fruits,
    so it feels like you are really eating them. We also launched aminoVITAL® CONNECT Joint Support.
    This health supplement’s main ingredients are six types of amino acids (serin, sodium aspartate, glutamic

                                                   - 67 -
acid, glycine, alanine, and proline) (4,000 mg), which are found in great abundance in collagen and are
reported to be effective in alleviating knee joint discomfort.
Furthermore, from the AQUASOLITA® series, we launched AQUASOLITA® and AQUASOLITA® jelly
with new labels after receiving labeling permission from the Consumer Affairs Agency for “Foods for
Special Dietary Uses” and “Foods for Medical Uses (Individual Evaluation form).” These products are
suitable for replenishing fluids and electrolytes in persons suffering mild dehydration due to heat
exhaustion or excessive sweating. It is an easy-to-drink oral rehydration solution made with our
ingredient formulation technologies, which leverage our unique Deliciousness Technology®.

—Fundamental foods—
We released Glyna® for sleep care and stress care, a food with function claims that contains two amino
acids: glycine, which helps with sleep care, and GABA, which helps with stress care. The sleep-support
drink market is also growing, so we responded to demand from consumers for a convenient sleep care
beverage by launching a Glyna® drink. In our development, we used the Ajinomoto Group’s unique target
quality design technology, AJI-PMap® to select the optimal flavor and fragrance for a sleep care drink to
be used before going to bed.

—Personal care ingredients—
In 1972, the Ajinomoto Group released Amisoft®, an amino acid-based surfactant made with glutamic
acid. Ever since then, for over half a century, we have been supplying diverse products for use as
ingredients in amino acid-derived cosmetics and toiletry products to over 5,000 cosmetics manufacturers
and other companies in 55 countries. The Ajinomoto Group’s personal care ingredient products, made
using “AminoScience,” are gentle on the skin, gentle to the environment, and have features such as
exceptional moisturization. They are widely used in skincare, haircare, makeup, and other products.
Leveraging our strengths as an ingredient manufacturer, we are also expanding our JINO brand of
skincare products specializing in cosmetic ingredients made with our own amino acids.
We updated our Amino Moist series of products in the JINO amino acid skincare brand and began selling
two types of essential lotion and two types of essential emulsion (a total of four types of products) from
our new JINO Moist Amino Enriched series, available only through e-commerce sites. These products use
a thorough moisturization approach based on our unique Amino Beauty TheoryTM, the fruit of long years
of skin science research by the Research Institute for Bioscience Products & Fine Chemicals of the
Company, and unique amino acid formulations that support aging care. We also launched ELDEW® FE-
01, a new product in our ELDEW® series of ingredients for skincare cosmetics. The amino acid-based
emollient ELDEW®PS series is designed to go onto the skin even more smoothly by suspending nano-
sized oil droplets in water using our nano-emulsion technologies, which are made possible by the use of a
unique formulation (patent pending).

—Feed-use amino acids—
AjiPro®-L, our lysine amino acid preparation for cows, supplements cows’ intake of amine acid lysine,
which is often lacking, simply by mixing it into feed. This preparation balances the amino acids in feed.
We began manufacturing and selling this product in North America in 2011. In 2015, we began selling it
in Japan, and it is now the top lysine amino acid preparation for cows, used around the world. Greenhouse
gasses (GHGs) from raising cattle, such as methane and nitrous oxide in cattle manure and burps,
accounts for roughly 9.5% of the world’s GHG emissions. It is a pressing issue, as it is one of the causes
of global warming. We have launched a global strategic partnership with Danone S.A. (France) to reduce
the GHG emissions from the company’s milk supply chain. In this partnership, our AjiPro®-L is used to
improve the efficiency with which amino acids in feed are absorbed by dairy cattle. This greatly lowers
feed costs and reduces a broad range of GHG emissions related to the raising of dairy cattle. We signed a
partnership agreement with Kagoshima Prefecture and livestock businesses within the prefecture with the
aims of reducing GHG emissions from raising livestock and dairy cattle while stimulating the industry,
and we are promoting green transformation (GX) strategies with local governments. GHG emissions
reduction projects using amino acids, which are at the heart of our solutions, have already been registered
as J-Credit Scheme methodologies. GHG emissions can be converted into credits, and this method of
reducing GHG emissions by using amino acids to improve livestock productivity is the only method for
reducing GHG emissions from manure and methane emissions from burps. We, along with Kagoshima



                                              - 68 -
    Prefecture, received the Consumer Affairs Agency Director’s Award in the 2024 Awards for Good
    Practices of Consumer-Oriented Management, held by the Consumer Affairs Agency.

    Research and development expenses for the Healthcare and Others segment amounted to ¥11,212 million.

(5) Corporate
    By backcasting from our future vision in the years from 2030 to 2050, we aim for business expansion in
    the fields which show promise for the future of the Ajinomoto Group, and carry out Group-wide research
    of related research topics, focus our resource investment, and engage in development work. In our Group-
    wide research, the Institute of Food Sciences and Technologies and the Research Institute for Bioscience
    Products & Fine Chemicals of the Company play a central role, coordinating with other research
    organizations in Japan and overseas to leverage pioneering research and technologies, developing new
    technologies and unique materials and ingredients for various businesses together with other research labs
    within the Group, and reinforcing fundamental technologies shared by different businesses.
    We are also increasing our investment in intangible assets. Firstly, our technology assets include
    “AminoScience,” represented by our Deliciousness Technology and cutting-edge bioscience and fine
    chemical technology. Going forward, we believe that digital capabilities will be vital to better meeting the
    needs and wants of our customers. We will increase our investment in human assets that match our
    customers and technologies to generate innovation, as well as in customer assets and organization assets
    that serve as the foundation of these assets.

    Open innovation
    We actively promote open innovation, and we believe that it is important to link it to companies, research
    organizations, and other organizations in Japan and overseas to create new and unprecedented value. Our
    innovation strategy teams help globally accelerate our innovation in growth areas of the Ajinomoto
    Group. They coordinate with various internal organizations (corporate venture capital, R&D, business
    divisions, etc.) and external partners across the globe to formulate and implement organic and inorganic
    growth strategies. These teams have begun activities from their Japanese, North American, Latin
    American, and ASEAN sites. In North America, they have established a site in the Boston area, which is a
    central part of the innovation ecosystem. Furthermore, to promote the creation of strategies for partnering
    with startups and the collection of state-of-the-art innovation information on a global scale, a new site was
    also set up in January 2024 in Silicon Valley (Palo Alto, California) in the US. The establishment of the
    US site was part of our efforts to globally expand our innovation strategy teams. These teams directly
    access the world’s state-of-the-art innovation information and activities and concentrate our intelligence
    functions (Search, Access & Partnering) for speedily deliberating and making decisions regarding
    investments, partnerships, M&As, etc., with the aim of realizing our growth strategies through the
    creation of next-generation business.

    Our main open innovation activities in FY2024 were as follows.

    —Healthcare area—
    In FY2023, we made Forge Biologics, Inc., a US-based gene therapy CDMO, into a wholly consolidated
    subsidiary. We will move forward with our transition to a business model that offers high added value by
    advancing into next-generation business fields, accelerate our growth in the healthcare area, and work to
    increase profitability in this area. We also completed our investment in Enhanced Medical Nutrition Inc.
    (Ontario), a Canadian surgical nutrition startup. Through this investment, we will reinforce our efforts to
    make further improvements to address patients’ nutritional challenges, in addition to the medical food
    business we have already operated through our consolidated subsidiaries, US-based Ajinomoto
    Cambrooke, Inc. and Nualtra Limited, which has sites in the UK and Ireland.




                                                   - 69 -
—Food & Wellness area—
The Company has developed the world’s first “electric seasoning” technology, a novel concept of
adjusting the taste of foods utilizing transcutaneous electrical stimulation, through joint research with
Project Associate Professor Hiromi Nakamura of the Junichi Rekimoto Laboratory, Interfaculty Initiative
in Information Studies, The University of Tokyo (currently Associate Professor, Tokyo City University)
and Project Professor Chinatsu Kasamatsu of the Institute for SDGs Promotion, Ochanomizu University
(currently Project Professor, Tokyo Kasei Gakuin University). “Electric seasoning” specifically refers to
the technology itself (rather than the device), developed to control taste through weak electrical
stimulation of the anterior part of the lower jaw and back of the neck. The results of this research, which
demonstrate that the tastes of various foods are enhanced through transcutaneous electrical stimulation,
have been published in Hypertension Research. Toward the achievement of its purpose of contributing to
the well-being of all human beings, our society and our planet with “AminoScience,” we are aiming to
extend the healthy life expectancy of one billion people by 2030. Leveraging the novel concept of
“electric seasoning,” it will contribute to healthy and comfortable lifestyles by enriching the foods eaten
by consumers, including those who need to reduce their salt intake.
In March 2024, we began offering the web-based Mirai Kondate® menu proposal service. This service
uses JANPS®: Japan Nutrient Profiling System, which was developed by the Company and is well-
tailored for the food culture of Japan, to propose nutritionally balanced menus with dishes users love. It
can be used to create eight-day long, nutritionally balanced “golden menus,” and “tsujitsuma (making-
ends-meet) menus” for a day following nutritionally unbalanced meals. Mirai Kondate® was redesigned
with content that is even easier for users to understand and use. We, along with ten other food
manufacturers and recipe video media operators, have participated in a nationwide project to propose
Tsujitsumashiawase®, a new method for practicing a nutritionally balanced diet. This project aims to
propose and raise awareness of Tsujitsumashiawase®, a specific method that can be used to enjoy a fun
and delicious diet while reducing the burden involved in thinking about how to maintain a good
nutritional balance, such as the feeling of obligation to balance nutrition or the feeling of guilt when you
eat what you want and your diet becomes unbalanced. The project assists in the realization of healthy
lives that are both physically and emotionally satisfying.
Furthermore, as part of our support for the improvement of employee health, the Company has developed
The Eat Well Check® program, which assists in improving lifestyle habits by providing nutritionally
balanced meals, advice from experts, and diet and exercise self-guidance using the Company’s own
proprietary diet improvement tools. We carried out a three-month pilot test of this program within our
company and found that its results were significant. We have considered using this program as a way to
transform behavior and improve health for employees whose workstyles and working conditions do not
allow them to use the internal canteens, to assist our health management efforts. Details regarding the
results of this research were presented at the 28th annual meeting of Japan Society of Metabolism and
Clinical Nutrition, held from January 17 to 19, 2025 at the Kyoto International Conference Center.
Furthermore, as an official JOC and JPC sponsor (contract categories: sauces & seasonings, dried soup,
nutritional supplements, frozen foods, coffee beans), the Company supplied Ajinomoto products and
menus developed in-house to TEAM JAPAN, the athletes representing Japan in the Paris 2024 Summer
Olympics & Paralympics (hereafter “the Paris 2024 Games”). We assisted with the overall conditioning
of athletes by improving their mental and physical health through “AminoScience.” During the Paris 2024
Games, we collaborated with the Japanese Olympic Committee (JOC) and the Japanese Paralympic
Committee (JPC) of the Japanese Para Sports Association to help keep TEAM JAPAN in tip-top
condition. At the Paris 2024 Paralympics, we operated Café Du Dashi together with the JPC for the
benefit of athletes representing Japan. We will continue to respect the ideals and diversity of athletes,
support their mental and physical health through “AminoScience,” and supports them in realizing their
well-being. Furthermore, we use the knowledge we gain through these activities to contribute to the well-
being of consumers.


—Green area—
We launched the new brand Atlr.72TM, which proposes new dietary lifestyles that actively make use of
environmentally-friendly ingredients (plant-based, cell-based, microorganism-based, etc.) and make the
bounty and beauty of nature part of everyday life, and we have begun business development of the brand
in Singapore. The first products in the brand are sweets made with air-based protein Solein®, which we
began selling for a limited time only in shops such as Singapore Takashimaya.


                                               - 70 -
We became a participating partner in the “Demonstration Survey for Restoration of Degraded
Agricultural Land in Brazil” project, one of the initiatives of the Japan-Brazil Green Partnership Initiative
(Japan-Brazil GPI) being conducted under the Japanese and Brazilian governments. We will supply
products utilizing our biostimulant development and production technologies for use in restoring
degraded land in a model farm in Brazil, making into farmland once again.
Furthermore, in response to calls by the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development
Organization (NEDO) for proposals for its Research and Development of Technologies to Promote
Biomanufacturing project, we proposed “the development of precision fermentation technologies that
would help protect the environment while stabilizing the food supply,” and this proposal was selected by
NEDO for implementation. We leverage our knowledge and technical superiority in the field of
fermentation production of useful substances such as amino acids to develop technologies for the efficient
fermentation production of target proteins. Specifically, we develop microorganisms that produce target
proteins, carry out rapid development of stable commercial production processes utilizing AI and
simulations, and conduct lifecycle assessment during the product development stage, with an eye towards
social implementation.

Sustainability
In 2024, the initiatives being carried out throughout the Ajinomoto Group were evaluated in a
sustainability study by France-based EcoVadis, whose mission is to provide sustainability evaluations
with the highest levels of trust among businesses around the world. We were awarded the Gold medal,
which is presented to the top 5% of companies evaluated. This was the first time in five years that we
were presented a Gold medal, following our previous selection in 2019. EcoVadis evaluates the corporate
sustainability of over 220 companies in over 180 countries from Environment, Labor & Human Rights,
Ethics, and Sustainable Procurement perspectives. Our most recent evaluation was the highest we have
ever received, which we believe is due to EcoVadis recognizing the Ajinomoto Group’s pioneering
sustainability initiatives and the comprehensiveness of our disclosures.
We have also been selected for the Dow Jones World Index, one of the Dow Jones Sustainability Indices,
which are global ESG stock indices, for 11 consecutive years. The index analyzes and evaluates the
world’s top companies based on governance and economic, environmental, and social criteria to select
companies with exceptional sustainability. In 2024, it examined 3,500 global leading companies and
selected 321 for inclusion in the index (including seven global companies and three Japanese companies
in the food products industry). In the environmental area, we received high scores in categories such as
energy, waste and pollutants, and climate strategy. In the social area, we received high scores in
categories such as human capital management, labor health and safety, and health and nutrition.
We have become a member of the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD)
(Switzerland). This international economic council, whose goal is to promote sustainable development,
was established in 1995 and has over 225 corporate members from around the world. Through this
council, the Ajinomoto Group is participating in Agriculture & Food Pathway activities and Climate
Imperative activities.
We were also selected by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) and Tokyo Stock
Exchange, Inc. (TSE) as one of their Sustainability Transformation (SX) Brands in 2024. Sustainability
Transformation (SX) is an initiative to improve corporate value in a long-term, sustainable manner by
thinking about the sustainability of both the company and society in a synchronized way and carrying out
the necessary management and businesses reforms to achieve this. The SX Brands project selects and
awards progressive companies that are enhancing their ability to create a source of funds for growth in a
sustainable manner, using SX to improve their corporate value. This year was the first year that METI and
TSE select SX Brands. The Company was selected as a result of high evaluations of our establishment of
a business model that leverages our unique “AminoScience,” which is one of our competitive advantages;
our selection of materiality from a long-term, multi-stakeholder perspective with an eye towards 2050;
our creation of a path toward the realization of our Purpose, contributing to the well-being of all human
beings, our society and our planet with “AminoScience,” through the two outcomes of reducing our
environmental impact and extending the healthy life expectancy, among other initiatives.
We also received the Minister of the Environment Award in the 2024 Food Loss and Waste Reduction
Promotion Awards, which are held by the Ministry of the Environment and the Consumer Affairs Agency
to recognize companies with exceptional initiatives that are effective in reducing food loss and waste and
have the potential for further ripple effects. We were evaluated positively for our TOO GOOD TO
WASTETM food loss and waste prevention project, which we launched in 2022 to promote the

                                               - 71 -
transformation of consumer behavior and to contribute to the creation of an ecosystem through
collaborations both inside and outside the company.
Furthermore, to combat the problem of marine plastic pollution, the Company, together with Kewpie
Corporation, has begun a collaborative project to recycle mayonnaise bottles that is one of the activities of
the Clean Ocean Material Alliance, a joint public and private sector platform that spans industry lines.
There have been few technical verification projects involving the closed-loop recycling of polyethylene
(PE) mayonnaise bottles in Japan, and we must gather large amounts of information and technical
expertise to build an evaluation system aimed at eventual social implementation. We will solve the
difficult issues by pooling the knowledge of the two companies that have many years of experience with
mayonnaise, and we will establish the technologies necessary for the social implementation of closed-
loop recycling.

Corporate research and development expenses amounted to ¥9,562 million.

(8) Share ownership plan for directors (and other officers) and employees
     The Company has introduced a Stock-based Remuneration Based on the Company’s Medium-term
     Earnings Performance (the “Stock-based Remuneration”), with the aim of achieving sustained medium-to
     long-term improvement in business performance and increasing corporate value of the Ajinomoto Group.
     Under this System, the Company contributes up to ¥2.2 billion to a stock-granting trust (the “Trust”), and
     the Trust acquires the Company’s shares. After the end of the three-year trust period, performance is
     assessed using a predetermined valuation index, and the Trust pays the Company’s shares and the amount
     equivalent to the conversion and disposal of the Company’s shares (the “Company’s Shares, etc.”) to the
     eligible persons. They must be Executive Officers (including those who concurrently serving as
     Directors) of the Company during the target period. The maximum number of the Company’s shares to be
     granted to the Eligible Executive Officers is 1.1 million.
     The number of the Company’s shares to be granted to the Executive Officers is calculated by multiplying
     the evaluation indicators calculated based on the target achievement rate and the assessment weighting for
     each evaluation indicator, by the amount of the pre-set medium-term performance-linked remuneration by
     officers’ ranks and then dividing the product by the closing price of the Company’s shares on March 31,
     2023 (¥2,303.0). (Shares less than 100 are rounded down.) Half of the compensation will be delivered in
     the form of Company shares, and the remaining 50% will be used for payment of income tax, etc.,
     therefore the Trust will convert this to cash by selling the shares on the market and then paying the
     amount equivalent to the conversion and disposal of the Company’s shares. Stock-based Remuneration
     Based on the Company’s Medium-term Earnings Performance is paid to non-residents of Japan in the
     form of cash compensation.
     Those who newly become Executive Officers during the target period will be paid the Company’s Shares,
     etc., calculated on a monthly pro-rata basis according to the duration of their term of office as an
     Executive Officer. In the event of a change in position due to promotion, etc., during the target period, the
     Company’s Shares, etc. will be paid by proportionally calculating the Company’s medium-term earnings
     performance valuation index in accordance with the duration of the term of office in the position before
     and after the change. If an Executive Officer retires along the way (excluding resignations for personal
     reasons contrary to the Company’s wishes), they will receive Company Shares, etc. on a monthly pro-rata
     basis according to the length of their tenure. However, in the event of death or becoming a non-resident of
     Japan, a cash amount equivalent to the disposal value of the number of the Company’s shares calculated
     on a monthly pro-rata basis according to the length of their tenure will be paid.
     The evaluation indicators, target values, and assessment weighing for the Stock-based Remuneration
     Based on the Company’s Medium-term Earnings Performance covering the three fiscal years beginning in
     FY2023, as resolved by the Compensation Committee on March 16, 2023, are as follows.

3. Dividend policy
   The Company’s basic policy is to pay dividends twice a year, an interim dividend and a year-end dividend,
   with the interim dividend determined by the Board of Directors and the year-end dividend determined by the
   General Meeting of Shareholders. The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that, except as otherwise provided for
   by laws and regulations, dividends from surplus and other matters set forth in respective items of Article 459,
   Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act may be determined by a resolution of the Board of Directors. While the
   Articles of Incorporation stipulate the payment of year-end dividends as described above, in principle, the
   payment of such dividends is determined by a resolution at a General Meeting of Shareholders, except in cases
   where infectious diseases or natural disasters may affect the holding and operation of the General Meeting of
   Shareholders.
   In the Medium-Term ASV Management 2030 Roadmap, the Company has declared a progressive dividend
   policy, indicating a policy of increasing or maintaining dividends without reducing them, and plans to pay an
   annual dividend of ¥80 (interim dividend ¥40) per share for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, an increase
   of ¥6 from the previous fiscal year. The Company’s standard dividend calculation method is based on
   normalized EPS (Note), which uses business profit less affected by extraordinary profit fluctuations such as
   from impairment losses.
   The Company will continue to work to further increase dividends by steadily increasing business profit, and
   the total return ratio (to profit attributable to owners of the parent company) for the three-year period is set at
   50% or more.
   The Company conducted a 2-for-1 stock split of its ordinary shares effective April 1, 2025, with a record date
   of March 31, 2025.
   Based on these factors, the Company plans to pay an annual dividend of ¥48 per share (with an interim
   dividend of ¥24 per share) for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026, which is ¥96 per share on a pre-split
   basis.
   Internal reserves will be allocated first to support organic growth, with M&A as the next priority to drive
   further business expansion. In addition, the Company will conduct flexible share repurchases within a net
   debt/EBITDA ratio of less than 2.0 ×.
   Note: Dividends based on normalized EPS = (Business profit × (1 − Ajinomoto Group standard tax rate at 27%)) / Total number
         of shares outstanding × Return coefficient at 35%

   Dividends from surplus for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025 are as follows.

4. Status of corporate governance, etc.
   (1) Overview of corporate governance
         (i)   Basic approach to corporate governance
               The Ajinomoto Group positions corporate governance as one of the most important aspects of its
               management foundation for strengthening the ASV Management and achieving our “Vision for
               2030.” Toward 2030, we accelerate the ASV Management for achieving “the extension of healthy
               life expectancy of one billion people” and “the reduction of our environmental impact by 50%”
               through initiatives of both resolving health and nutritional issues linked by food systems and
               promoting sustainability. Furthermore, in order to enhance the effectiveness of ASV Management,
               we select a “Company with Three Committees” that clearly separate supervision and execution by
               balancing “supervision of appropriate execution that reflects the opinions of stakeholders” and
               “business execution with a sense of speed.” In order to ensure the sustainable enhancement of
               corporate value over the medium to long term, the Board of Directors, which consists of a variety of
               Directors, indicates a major direction by discussing and examining important management matters
               that greatly affect our corporate value, supports risk-taking in execution, and appropriately
               supervises execution by verifying the validity of execution processes and results. On the other hand,
               the execution, the Chief Executive Officer who has been greatly delegated authority from the Board
               of Directors will take the lead in making decisions for important business execution at the Executive
               Committee, will realize sustainable enhancement of corporate value as One Team. In order to closely
               communicate between the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee, governance rules are
               established based on the Company’s approach to enhance corporate value, proposals and reports are
               made from the Executive Committee to the Board of Directors, and deliberations and resolutions are
               made by the Board of Directors.
               Recently, in the changes in the external environment comprehensive risk management is important
               than ever. We honestly comply with the Ajinomoto Group Policy (hereinafter, “AGP”) that shows
               the ideal way of thinking and action that Ajinomoto Group companies and their officers and
               employees should comply with, continue to develop and properly operate our internal control
               system, strengthen our system that considers sustainability as an active risk-taking system, and
               continuously enhance our corporate value.

  processes and results. Additionally, through the ASV Management, the Company works with stakeholders

                                                       - 92 -
< Business execution/Executive Committee >

 The Representative Executive Officer & President who has been greatly delegated authority from the
 Board of Directors takes the lead in making decisions for important business execution at the Executive
 Committee, and the Company will realize sustainable enhancement of corporate value as One Team.
 The Representative Executive Officer & President, serving as Chief Executive Officer (CEO), oversees
 and executes the Company’s business operations. Executive Officers execute the Company’s business
 operations in accordance with the resolutions of the Board of Directors, with responsibilities divided
 among them.
 The Executive Committee will realize prompt and appropriate business execution with a team centered on
 the Chief Executive Officer based on the major directions and mandates indicated by the Board of
 Directors. Deliberations and resolutions on basic plans, policies, and other important matters related to
 business execution will be described in the minutes along with the approval and disapproval of the
 members of the Executive Committee. In addition, proposals and reports to the Board of Directors are
 conducted in accordance with the Regulations on Board of Directors and the Minor Regulations on Board
 of Directors, and close communication is made so that the agenda of the Board of Directors can be set
 systematically and effectively. Members of the Executive Committee are consisted of the Representative
 Executive Officer & President and the other Executive Officers appointed by the Representative Executive
 Officer & President, and approved by the Board of Directors.
 The Company’s business management organizations are divided into the Corporate Division, Food
 Products Division, and Bio & Fine Chemicals Division. Each organization carries out the operations
 delegated to it under the direction and supervision of the Executive Officer in charge. Each business
 operation organization carries out its prescribed operations according to the directions and supervision of
 the Executive Officer responsible. In order to execute business strategically in specific functions across the
 business operation organizations, we have appointed a CDO, who oversees the Company’s digital
 transformation as the head of digital technology, a CXO, who oversees the improvement of organizational
 strengths through operational transformation as the head of companywide operational transformation; and
 a CIO, who oversees new business model creation as the head of business model transformation, to head
 up these respective functions.
 The internal rules on decision-making procedures of the Ajinomoto Group, which classify each business
 operational organization of the Group (including Group companies) into a hierarchy from the standpoint of
 their roles, clarify approval criteria. In this manner, Ajinomoto Co., Inc. strives to speed up decision
 making and raise the efficiencies of its organizational management as well as streamline operations across
 the entire Group by reinforcing the management functions of the Board of Directors and further delegating
 authority to the Executive Committee.




                                                 - 93 -
< Internal control, risk management and sustainability >
- Business Conduct Committee
  The Business Conduct Committee has been established to strengthen the Ajinomoto Group’s management
  base and enhance corporate value by fostering an open corporate culture and building a corporate structure
  that is resistant to crises, etc., by raising compliance awareness and instilling AGP. In addition, the
  Business Conduct Committee thoroughly disseminate AGP, determine and implement various measures to
  respond promptly and appropriately to crises, etc., disseminate information to raise compliance awareness,
  grasp trends and respond from the viewpoint of compliance, and implement smooth and prompt responses
  and appropriate resolution.


- Sustainability Committee
  The Sustainability Committee has been established as a subordinate body of the Executive Committee to
  promote sustainability management. The Sustainability Committee works with the Risk Management
  Committee to select and identify risks and opportunities based on materiality, as well as assess their impact
  on the Ajinomoto Group, making proposals to the Executive Committee. The Committee then formulates
  countermeasures against risks and opportunities relevant to sustainability and manages their progress. In
  addition, the Sustainability Committee formulates the entire Ajinomoto Group’s sustainability strategy,
  promotes action themes (nutrition, environment, and society) based on this strategy, makes proposals and
  provides support for business plans from a sustainability viewpoint, and compiles internal information on
  ESG.


- Risk Management Committee
  The Risk Management Committee has been established as a subordinate body of the Executive Committee
  in order to identify risks, which interfere the achievement of the “Purpose-Driven Management by
  Medium-Term ASV Initiatives,” as well as in order to establish and implement measures for risk
  management. The Risk Management Committee works with the Sustainability Committee to select and
  identify risks and opportunities based on materiality as well as assess their impact on the Ajinomoto
  Group, making proposals to the Executive Committee. Additionally, the Committee considers various
  measures for risk management, particularly for risks that management should take the initiative to address
  (such as geographical risks and information security risks), and formulates risk management measures and
  manages their progress in order to realize a strong corporate structure capable of responding promptly and
  appropriately to risks and crises.


- Investment, Loan and Business Scrutiny Committee
  The Investment, Loan, and Business Scrutiny Committee carries out multifaceted reviews of investment
  and loan decisions, prior to deliberations by the Executive Committee.


- M&A Committee
  The M&A Committee carries out multifaceted reviews of M&A deals prior to deliberations by the
  Executive Committee.

         2)   Reasons for adoption of current corporate governance system
               The Ajinomoto Group positions corporate governance as one of the most important aspects of its
               management foundation for strengthening ASV Management and achieving its 2030 vision. Toward
               2030, we will accelerate our ASV Management in order to realize our goals of “extending the
               healthy life expectancy of one billion people” and “reducing our environmental impact by 50%” by
               promoting sustainability in conjunction with solutions to health and nutritional issues, which are
               connected through food systems. Furthermore, to enhance the effectiveness of ASV Management,
               we select a Company with Three Committees that clearly separate supervision and execution by
               balancing “supervision of appropriate execution that reflects the opinions of stakeholders” and
               “business execution with a sense of speed.”
         3)   Views on the abilities and diversity of the Board of Directors as a whole
               The Company has a basic policy which considers the number of members, the percentage of Internal
               Directors and Independent Outside Directors, the percentage of persons who concurrently serve as
               Executive Officers, individual experience, abilities, insights, internationality, gender, race, ethnic
               group, nationality, country of origin and cultural background, etc., for the Board of Directors
               composed of Independent Outside Directors who can objectively supervise business execution from
               an independent standpoint, Internal Directors who concurrently serve as Executive Officers
               including the CEO, and Internal Directors who are members of the Audit Committee (Standing).
               The Board of Directors is composed of directors possessing the specialties, expertise and experience
               outlined in the following table, and it works with stakeholders and others to resolve social issues,
               contributes to the realization of a sustainable society, and is committed to sustainable enhancement
               of corporate value, based on the Company’s purpose of “contributing to the well-being of all human
               beings, our society and our planet with ‘AminoScience’.”
               In addition, in order to promote the separation of supervision and execution and further enhance the
               effectiveness of the management oversight function by the Board of Directors, the Independent
               Outside Directors shall occupy a majority, and the Chair of the Board shall be the Independent
               Outside Director.

         4)   Status of systems developed to ensure proper business operations
               The Basic Policy on the Internal Control System, as resolved by the Board of Directors is as
               follows.

               1. System to Ensure that the Execution of Duties by Executive Officers and Employees of the Company Complies
                  with Laws and Regulations as well as the Articles of Incorporation

                 (1) By appointing an Independent Outside Director who can objectively supervise the execution of the
                     Company’s business from an independent standpoint, consisting a majority of the Board of Directors as
                      Outside Directors, and appointing the Chairperson of the Board of Directors as an Outside Director, the
                      Board of Directors shall strengthen the supervisory function for the execution of duties by Executive
                      Officers and employees of the Board of Directors, and ensure the appropriateness of business execution.

                 (2) Establish the Nomination Committee and the Compensation Committee, both with a majority of members
                     comprising Outside Directors, as voluntary committees of the Board of Directors in order to enhance the
                      transparency and objectivity of decisions related to the nomination of Directors, and the compensation of
                      Directors and corporate Executive Officers.

                 (3) The Audit Committee composed of Outside Directors and Internal Directors who supervise business
                      execution based on a deep understanding of the Company’s business, with a majority of the chairperson and
                      committee members as Outside Directors, and auditing the legality and appropriateness of Company’s
                      business execution by Executive Officers, plays an important role in the function of “supervision of business
                      execution,” and auditing the execution of the duties by Directors. The Audit Committee inspects the minutes
                      of the Nomination Committee and the Compensation Committee.


                                                                - 100 -
  (4) The Ajinomoto Group Policies (AGP) are established to illustrate the beliefs and behaviors which the
      companies in the Ajinomoto Group and each individual who works there should uphold, and to provide a
      written commitment to all of our stakeholders that they will uphold them.

  (5) The Business Conduct Committee, chaired by a member of the Executive Committee nominated by the
      Representative Executive Officer & President, checks management activities from the perspective of
      compliance, and seeks to make the AGP well known across the Ajinomoto Group in cooperation with
      relevant divisions, including providing support and coordinating activities to make the AGP prevail
      throughout the Ajinomoto Group companies.

  (6) The Business Conduct Committee seeks to enhance the awareness of compliance and promote the
      penetration of the AGP through the continuous implementation of education and training activities to help
      foster an open and friendly corporate culture.

  (7) The Business Conduct Committee establishes the desk within its secretariat to receive whistle-blowing as
      well as the desk to receive whistle-blowing outside the Company. Relevant internal divisions promptly
      respond to whistleblowing, report the outcome of handling such whistle-blowing to the Business Conduct
      Committee, the Executive Committee, and the Board of Directors in order to prevent recurrence of
      problems.

  (8) The Internal Auditing Dept. conducts audit on business of operational organizations and Ajinomoto Group
      companies, reports the audit results to the Representative Executive Officer & President and the Audit
      Committee (Double Report), instructs organizations audited to correct matters pointed out in the audit, and
      checks on the implementation status of such corrections. Provided, however, that in order to ensure the
      independence of audits and maintain an effective and efficient auditing system, the latter shall be given
      priority in the event that the directions of the Representative Executive Officer & President conflict with the
      directions of the Audit Committee, in the directions of audit function. In order to ensure the reliability of
      financial reporting, the Internal Auditing Dept. assesses the internal control over financial reporting, reports
      the assessment results to the Representative Executive Officer & President and the Audit Committee,
      notifies organizations assessed of the assessment results, and instructs them to correct inadequacies, if any.
      Provided, however, that the latter shall be given priority in the event that the directions of the Representative
      Executive Officer & President conflict with the directions of the Audit Committee, in the directions of audit
      function. The Internal Auditing Dept. conducts investigations and audits at the direction of the Audit
      Committee.

2. System Concerning the Storage and Management of Information Related to the Execution of Duties by
   Executive Officers of the Company

      Store and manage documents and electronic records that record information related to the execution of
      duties by Executive Officers and Directors, including minutes of Board of Directors meetings, minutes of
      Executive Committee meetings, documents on decision-making, and minutes of various meetings in
      accordance with laws and regulations, and company regulations.

3. Regulations and Other Systems Concerning Management of Risk of Losses of the Company

  (1) The Risk Management Committee works with the Sustainability Committee to select and identify risks and
      opportunities based on materiality as well as assess their impact on the Ajinomoto Group, making proposals
      to the Executive Committee. Additionally, the committee formulates various measures for risk management,
      particularly for risks that management should take the initiative to address (such as geographical risks and
      information security risks), and formulates risk management measures and manages their progress in order
      to realize a strong corporate structure capable of responding promptly and appropriately to risks and crises.




                                              - 101 -
  (2) The Sustainability Committee works with the Risk Management Committee to select and identify risks and
      opportunities based on materiality, as well as assess their impact on the Ajinomoto Group, making proposals
      to the Executive Committee. The committee then formulates countermeasures against risks and opportunities
      relevant to sustainability and manages their progress. In addition, the Sustainability Committee formulates
      the entire Ajinomoto Group’s sustainability strategy, promotes action themes (nutrition, environment, and
      society) based on this strategy, makes proposals and provides support for business plans from a sustainability
      viewpoint, and compiles internal information on ESG.

  (3) In the event of a crisis, establish task forces, etc., at relevant organizations, give the highest priority to
      human life, and strive to minimize losses to the Ajinomoto Group.

4. System to Ensure that the Execution of Duties by Executive Officers of the Company Is Performed Efficiently

  (1) The Board of Directors meets once a month, in principle, to discuss and make decisions on important
      matters set forth in laws and regulations and the Articles of Incorporation as well as “Board of Directors
      Regulations,” etc., and supervises the execution of duties by Directors and Executive Officers.

  (2) The Executive Committee, which comprises the Representative Executive Officer and other Executive
      Officers nominated by the Representative Executive Officer, meets three times a month, in principle, to
      discuss and make decisions on important matters concerning the Company and the Ajinomoto Group set
      forth in “Global Governance Regulations.”

  (3) Clarify the scope of decision-making by the Board of Directors, the Executive Committee, Executive
      Officers and specified Ajinomoto Group companies, and proceed with the delegation of authority through
      the development, operation and review of company regulations.

  (4) Documents and other materials are submitted in electronic files to the Board of Directors and the Executive
      Committee in order to ensure the efficient operation of the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee.

5. System to Ensure the Appropriate Operation of Ajinomoto Group Companies

  (1) System related to reports to the Company related to the execution of duties by Directors of Ajinomoto Group
      companies

       Operating organizations are responsible for supervision of Ajinomoto Group companies they are in charge
       of in accordance with “Global Governance Regulations,” request reports related to the execution of duties
       by Directors of Ajinomoto Group companies, and refer important matters to decision-making by Executive
       Officers, the Executive Committee or the Board of Directors of the Company.

  (2) Regulations and other systems concerning management of risk of losses of Ajinomoto Group companies

       i. Make Ajinomoto Group companies enforce company regulations with the same effects as Ajinomoto
          Group common regulations depending on their respective business operations and management
          environments, etc.

       ii. In the event of a crisis at an Ajinomoto Group company, set up a task force, etc., as necessary and
          provide support in order to minimize losses to the Ajinomoto Group.

  (3) System to ensure that the execution of duties by Directors of Ajinomoto Group companies is performed
      efficiently

       i. Clarify the basic policy related to the supervision of Ajinomoto Group companies, make Ajinomoto
          Group companies enforce company regulations with the same effects as Ajinomoto Group common
          regulations, and provide guidance and support to ensure that the company regulations are operated
          effectively

       ii. Conduct the appropriate delegation of authority to specified Ajinomoto Group companies in accordance
          with “Global Governance Regulations.”

  (4) System to ensure that the execution of duties by officers and employees of Ajinomoto Group companies
      complies with laws and regulations as well as the Articles of Incorporation


                                                - 102 -
      i. Make Ajinomoto Group companies implement the AGP and have their officers and employees, etc.
         thoroughly comply with laws and regulations as well as the AGP.

      ii. Thoroughly make it widely known that officers and employees, etc. of Ajinomoto Group companies can
         make use of the desks to accept whistle-blowing set up in and outside the Company.

      iii. The Internal Auditing Dept. of the Company conducts audit on management and operations of Ajinomoto
         Group companies as well as assessment of the internal control over financial reporting.

      iv. At important Ajinomoto Group companies, even when they do not fall under the category of “Large
         Company” as defined by the Companies Act, assign Audit & Supervisory Board members (standing) in
         order to enhance the audit function.

6. System to Ensure that the Audit by Audit Committee of the Company Is Conducted Effectively

  (1) Matters concerning employees, etc. who assist in the execution of duties by Audit Committee

      i. The Audit Committee is independently involved in the selection and evaluation of Executive Officers in
         charge of the Internal Control and Audit Committee and the General Manager of the Internal Auditing
         Dept. to assist in their duties.

      ii. Within the Internal Auditing Dept., the Audit Committee staff necessary to assist the Audit Committee in
         its duties. The Audit Committee shall proactively engage in personnel evaluations, personnel changes,
         and disciplinary actions of the Audit Committee staff to enhance their independence from Executive
         Officers and ensure the effectiveness of the Audit Committee’s instructions to the Audit Committee staff.

  (2) System concerning reports to Audit Committee

      i. Executive Officers, when it detects facts that may cause significant losses to the Company or Ajinomoto
         Group companies, immediately reports them to the Member of the Audit Committee.

      ii. Employees of the Company as well as Directors, Audit & Supervisory Board members, and employees
          of Ajinomoto Group companies comply with requests for regular and non-regular reports from the
         Member of the Audit Committee or the Audit Committee of the Company. When they detect facts that
         may cause significant losses to the Company or Ajinomoto Group companies and they consider them as
         requiring urgent attention, they may report such facts directly to the Member of the Audit Committee or
         the Audit Committee of the Company.

      iii. Establish the “Hotline to Audit Committee” as the dedicated desk to report suspicions about the direct
         involvement in wrongdoing by officers of Ajinomoto Group companies.

      iv. No disadvantageous treatment is guaranteed for those who made reports in i. and ii. or whistleblowing
          for iii. for making such reports or whistle-blowing. This policy is thoroughly enforced at Ajinomoto
         Group companies.

  (3) Policy related to the handling of audit expenses

      i. The Company bears expenses required by the execution of duties of Audit Committee (including
         expenses related to the necessary solicitation of opinions from lawyers and other outside experts).

      ii. Regarding the audit-related expenses in i., make it a rule to set an annual budget and pay for expenses
          that arises in the year from the budget. However, expenses urgently or additionally required in relation to
         audit are also borne outside the predetermined annual budget.

  (4) Other systems to ensure that the audit by Audit Committee is conducted effectively




                                                - 103 -
      i. Executive Officers make arrangements to allow Members of Audit Committee to attend important
          meetings held at operating organizations and offer other cooperation necessary for the execution of duties
          by Audit Committee, including submission of minutes of such meetings.

      ii. The Representative Executive Officer & President, other Executive Officers, and Member of Audit
          Committee or Audit Committee exchange information, regularly or on a non-regular basis, on
          compliance, risk management efforts and other management issues at the Company and Ajinomoto
          Group companies, and ensure better communication between Executive Officers, and Audit Committee.

7. System for the elimination of antisocial forces

  The Company clearly states to the AGP that we strictly avoid any involvement with organized antisocial forces,
  which pose a threat to civic order and safety, stand resolutely against organized antisocial forces and refuse any
   and all inappropriate demands, and the Business Conduct Committee seeks to make the AGP well known across
   the Ajinomoto Group in cooperation with relevant divisions, including providing support and coordinating
   activities to make the AGP prevail throughout the Ajinomoto Group companies.




                                              - 104 -
5)   Overview of management status of systems to ensure proper business operations
     Based on the Basic Policy on the Internal Control System, the Company has developed and properly
     operated an internal control system. The main initiatives conducted during the fiscal year ended
     March 31, 2025 were as indicated below.

     1. Compliance initiatives

       (1) The Business Conduct Committee makes continuous efforts to ensure thorough compliance with the
           Ajinomoto Group Policies (AGP). During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, as well, the AGP Worksite
           Meeting were held at workplaces nationwide (33 sessions were held within the Company). These study
           sessions provided opportunities to promote greater understanding of AGP and to inspect compliance risks in
           workplaces, and we identified compliance issues in workplaces and elicited opinions on Company-wide
           initiatives. The Company also conducted 12 e-learning sessions (with a separate theme each month) and
           conducted four group training sessions. These activities were reported at the Business Conduct Committee
           meetings held four times per year, and the Committee reported the results of the activities to the Executive
           Committee and the Board of Directors.

       (2) During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, the Internal Auditing Dept. audited operations for the
           Company’s business operation organizations and Group companies (at a total of 29 sites).

     2. Risk management initiatives

       (1) The Risk Management Committee met four times. It identified the following as risks that have not yet
           manifested themselves and that management should take the initiative in addressing (management risks):
           cyberattacks by outside parties, limitations on access to Chinese markets due to a deterioration in the
           relationship between the United States and China, the escalation of the Taiwan Strait issue, and major
           earthquake or flooding damage in the Tokyo metropolitan area. It also proposed countermeasures for
           addressing these risks.

       (2) The Sustainability Committee met five times. It coordinated with personnel in business divisions, regional
           headquarters, and corporate departments to confirm significant company-wide risks and opportunities based
           on materialities, initiatives for addressing them, related KPIs, and to share information on the reduction of
           greenhouse gasses, the reduction of plastic waste, nutritional improvements, measures for addressing human
           rights and other issues, and case examples of initiatives.

       (3) The Investment, Loan, and Business Scrutiny Committee met seven times. The M&A Committee met five
           times to deliberate M&As, two times to follow up on PMI for acquired companies, and one time to revise
           the M&A Committee Rules. The Quality Assurance Committee and the Occupational Safety and Health
           Committee each met two times, reviewed the Group’s overall activities, and confirmed its initiatives for
           addressing critical issues.

     3. Global governance initiatives (governance system with driving force and efficiency)

       (1) The Board of Directors met 18 times. It continuously worked to increase Board operation efficiency.
           Furthermore, it reviewed the “Seven Important Management Matters” that could have a significant impact
           on corporate value over the medium-to long-term, which are matters that should be discussed by the Board
           of Directors, in order to achieve “Where We Want To Be” set forth in the Medium-Term ASV Initiatives
           2030 Roadmap.

       (2) The Executive Committee met 37 times. It revised the Committee’s code of conduct and reported on,
           discussed, and made decisions regarding important matters related to the Company and the Group stipulated
           in the Global Governance Regulations.

       (3) The Global Governance Regulations were revised to further strengthen global governance.

     4. Initiatives related to auditing by the Audit Committee




                                                   - 105 -
           (1) As of March 31, 2025, nine personnel (seven full-time personnel and two personnel with concurrent
               positions) were assigned as staff to assist the Audit Committee in its duties. They have been given access
               privileges to essential Company information, perform comprehensive monitoring when appropriate, and
               coordinate with the Internal Auditing Dept. to ensure the effectiveness of auditing by the Audit Committee.
               The Audit Committee met 16 times during the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025.

           (2) The General Manager of the Internal Auditing Dept. reported the results of the internal audit to the Audit
               Committee Communication Committee meeting and reported on internal audit activities and evaluations of
               internal control related to financial reporting to the Audit Committee once every three months. They also
               responded to reporting requests and conducted hearings as necessary. When matters with the potential to
               cause significant losses for the Company or Group companies are discovered, they are reported in turn to
               Members of the Audit Committee, but no such matters were discovered during the fiscal year ended March
               31, 2025.


6)       Summary of Limited Liability Agreements
     The Company has entered into an agreement with Independent Outside Directors to limit their
     liability for damages under Article 427, Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act. Financial limitations on
     liability for damage based on this Agreement shall be the aggregate amount as stipulated in the
     respective items of Article 425, Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act.

7)       Summary of limited liability agreements for officers, etc.
     The Company has concluded a liability insurance policy for officers, etc., with an insurance company,
     as stipulated in Article 430-3, Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act. If a claim for damages is filed by a
     shareholder or a third party, those damages such as damages and dispute costs that the insured is to
     bear will be covered by the insurance policy. The persons insured by the liability policy are the
     Directors and Executive Officers of the Company, and the Directors, Audit & Supervisory Board
     Members and Corporate Officers of the Company’s subsidiaries. The Company will bear all premium
     payments for the insurance policy. The insurance policy will be renewed in September 2025.

8)       Provisions in the Articles of Incorporation concerning Directors
     -      Number of Directors
            The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that the Company shall have 12 Directors or less.
     -      Requirements for resolutions on the election of Directors
            The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that resolutions on the election of Directors shall be
            decided by shareholders who have one third or more of the voting rights of shareholders entitled
            to exercise their voting rights being in attendance at the Ordinary General Meeting of
            Shareholders and when a majority of the votes of such shareholders in attendance are in
            agreement. The Articles of Incorporation also stipulate that resolutions on the election of
            Directors shall not be conducted by cumulative voting.

9)       Matters for resolution by the General Meeting of Shareholders that can be resolved on by the Board
         of Directors
     -      Purchase of treasury stock
            The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that pursuant to Article 165, Paragraph 2 of the
            Companies Act, the Company may acquire its own shares through market transactions, etc. by
            resolution of the Board of Directors. This provision enables the Company to flexibly repurchase
            treasury stock to improve shareholder returns and capital efficiency, and to replenish any
            shortfall of treasury stock under the additional purchase program for shares less than one unit.
     -       Distribution of surplus, etc.
            The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that, in order to flexibly return profits to shareholders and
            implement capital policy, the Company may, by resolution of the Board of Directors, determine
            matters stipulated in respective items of Article 459, Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act,


                                                      - 106 -
       including the distribution of surplus. They also stipulate that dividends of surplus may be paid to
       shareholders or registered share pledgees recorded in the final shareholders’ register as of March
       31 or September 30 each year. Except in cases where infectious diseases or natural disasters may
       affect the holding and operation of the General Meeting of Shareholders, it is the Company’s
       policy that year-end dividends of surplus shall, in principle, be subject to resolution at the
       General Meeting of Shareholders.

10) Requirements for special resolutions of the General Meeting of Shareholders
    The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that special resolutions of the General Meeting of
    Shareholders, as provided in Article 309, Paragraph 2 of the Companies Act, require the attendance
    of shareholders holding one-third or more of the total voting rights exercisable, and the approval of
    two-thirds or more of the voting rights of the shareholders present. The purpose of this is to
    facilitate the operation of the Meeting of Shareholders by providing an easier quorum requirement
    for special resolutions at the General Meeting of Shareholders.
