                                                                - 131 -
(ii) Independent Outside Directors
   1.   Number of Independent Outside Directors
        The Company has 6 Independent Outside Directors.
   2.   Personal, capital and business relationships and other interests with Independent Outside
        Directors
        This information is as described in “(1) Overview of corporate governance (i) Basic approach to
        corporate governance,” and “(ii) 1) <Board of Directors and Committees>” and “(3) Views on the
        abilities and diversity of the Board of Directors as a whole.” The number of shares of the
        Company held by each Independent Outside Director is shown in the table in “(2) Status of
        officers (i) Lists of officers.”
   3.   Details regarding the function and role of Independent Outside Directors in corporate governance
        and the criteria or policy regarding their independence
        The Company has the basic policy, considering the number of members, the percentage of
        Internal Directors and Independent Outside Directors, the percentage of persons who
        concurrently serve as Directors and Executive Officers, individual experiences, abilities, insights,
        internationality, gender, race, ethnicity, nationality, country of origin, cultural background, etc.,
        for the Board of Directors composed of Independent Outside Directors who can objectively
        supervise business execution from an independent standpoint, Internal Directors who
        concurrently serve as Executive Officers including Chief Executive Officer, and Internal
        Directors who are Member of the Audit Committee (Standing). In addition, in order to promote
        the separation of supervision and execution and further enhance the effectiveness of the
        management oversight function by the Board of Directors, the Independent Outside Directors
        shall occupy a majority, and the Chair of the Board of Directors shall be the Independent Outside
        Director.
        There are no special interests between the Independent Outside Directors and the Company, and
        the Company has determined that the Independent Outside Directors have the independence
        necessary to fulfill their functions and roles.
        Mr. George Nakayama had served as Representative Director and Chairperson of Daiichi Sankyo
        Co., Ltd. Until June 2020 and has served as full-time advisor of the same company since June of
        the same year. In addition, Ajinomoto Co., Inc. had a business relationship in the past with
        Daiichi Sankyo Co., Ltd. However, there were no such interactions in the fiscal year ended
        March 31, 2025. Therefore, Mr. Nakayama fulfills the requirements of independence to serve as
        an Independent Outside Director of Ajinomoto Co., Inc.
        The Company’s Standards for Determining the Independence of Outside Directors are as follows.
        Outside Directors must not fall under any of the following categories to be considered independent.
        (1) Said person regards the Company as a key customer, or is an executive officer for such a party.
        (2) Said person is a key customer of the Company, or is an executive officer for such a party.
        (3) Said person is a consultant, accounting specialist or legal specialist who has received substantial monetary or
            other assets (other than director compensation) from the Company. (if the person receiving said assets is a
            corporate entity, association, or other such organization, this stipulation extends to members of that
            organization.)
        (4) Said person who falls under criteria (1), (2), or (3) above at any time within a one-year period before the
            proposed appointment.
        (5) Said person is a relative (a relative up through the second degree of kinship) of any person (other than those
            deemed unimportant) falling under criteria 1), 2), or 3) below.
            1) A person falling under criteria (1), (2), (3), or (4) above.
            2) A person who is an executive officer of a subsidiary of the Company.
            3) A person who falls under criteria 2) above or is an executive officer of the Company, at any time within a
               one-year period before the proposed appointment.




                                                   - 132 -
        Notes:
        1. A person who “regards the Company as a key customer,” refers to a person who, within the most recent
           business year, received from the Company an amount corresponding to 2% of that party’s annual consolidated
           sales or ¥100 million, whichever is higher.
        2. A person who is “a key customer of the Company,” refers to a person who, within the most recent business
           year, paid to the Company an amount corresponding to 2% of our annual consolidated sales or ¥100 million,
           whichever is higher.
        3. A person who “has received substantial monetary or other assets from the Company,” refers to a person who,
            within the most recent business year, has received from the Company monies/property in an amount
            corresponding to 2% of that party’s sales/ total revenues or ¥10 million, whichever is higher.

        As members of the Board of Directors, Independent Outside Directors provide major direction by

        Corporate Governance of Ajinomoto Co., Inc., Independent Outside Directors work in

        details regarding coordination with internal auditing, Audit Committee auditing, and accounting

3. Main activities of Audit Committee members
    The Audit Committee operates under the basic policy of “Contributing to the enhancement of
    corporate value by preventing corporate misconduct and ensuring lawful and appropriate
    business execution by the Group through audits of the duties performed by Directors and
    Executive Officers, thereby securing sound and sustainable growth of the Group, establishing
    high-quality corporate governance that considers the interests of various stakeholders, and
    earning the trust of society.” During the current fiscal year, the Audit Committee focused on the
    following three key areas: 1) enhancing execution capabilities related to the 2030 Roadmap and
    refining the Roadmap appropriately in response to internal and external environmental changes;
    2) building management foundations, including group-wide governance frameworks; and 3)
    reviewing IT governance initiatives and responses to geopolitical risks related to raw material
    procurement, logistics, and other factors, as well as efforts toward human rights risk
    management and sustainability-related disclosures.
 1) Monitoring the status of governance
    Audit Committee members attended meetings of the Board of Directors, auditing the
    proceedings and resolutions, and expressing their opinions when necessary. Full-time Audit

                                             - 136 -
  Committee members participated in key internal meetings and committees, such as the
  Executive Committee and the Business Conduct Committee. Some Independent Outside
  Directors serving as Audit Committee members also serve concurrently as members of the
  Nomination Committee and the Compensation Committee.
  All Audit Committee members held quarterly meetings, four times a year, with the
  Representative Executive Officer & President and the Executive Officer & Senior Vice
  President in charge of corporate affairs. Full-time Audit Committee members also held
  individual meetings with Executive Officers to exchange views on issues in their respective
  areas of responsibility. Where necessary, the Audit Committee provided recommendations to
  enhance the effectiveness of corporate governance based on these dialogues. The Audit
  Committee also received reports from and engaged in opinion exchanges with Directors,
  Executive Officers, and department heads as necessary.
  The Audit Committee monitored the operation of the governance framework, including the
  delegation of management execution to Executive Officers and the exercise of appropriate
  supervisory functions by the Board of Directors, in accordance with the Regulations of the
  Board of Directors and the Group Shared Policy on Governance (GGP), and reported and
  provided its opinions to the Board of Directors. The status of GGP-related decision-making
  operations was continuously monitored, shared and confirmed by the Audit Committee, and
  status updates and recommendations were provided during quarterly meetings with the
  Representative Executive Officer & President and the Executive Officer & Senior Vice
  President in charge of corporate affairs. In March 2025, the Audit Committee received a report
  from management on the results of the effectiveness verification conducted regarding the
  operation of the internal control system during FY2024 and offered recommendations aimed at
  continuous improvement.
2) Addressing risks
  For risks related to safety, quality, environment, information management (including personal
  information), and labor management, full-time Audit Committee members attended the
  Business Conduct Committee, the Sustainability Committee, and the Risk Management
  Committee to monitor compliance and risk management initiatives.
  The Audit Committee also continued monitoring the implementation of the whistleblowing
  system. Through the Audit Committee Hotline, which plays a key role in the system, Audit
  Committee members directly responded to reports concerning officers, including those of group
  companies. The status of these responses is deliberated and reported by the Audit Committee
  and subsequently reported to the Board of Directors.
3) Audits and investigations
  While making full use of internal audits conducted by the internal auditing department, Audit
  Committee members also engaged directly in audit activities to enhance the effectiveness of
  management audits through a “hybrid audit” approach. In the current fiscal year, audits and
  investigations were conducted at 20 domestic and overseas group company sites, in
  combination with departmental audits. Recommendations and proposals were made from the
  perspectives of management, human resources, finance, governance, and internal control. The
  results of these audits and investigations were shared at the Audit Committee Communication
  Meetings and subsequently reported to the Board of Directors.

(ii) Status of internal audits
   1. Purpose of internal audits
        The purpose of internal audits at the Company is to contribute to the achievement of
        management objectives, the strengthening of corporate governance, and the enhancement of
        public trust. This is accomplished by the internal auditing department independently evaluating
        the adequacy and effectiveness of governance, risk management, and internal control processes
        within the Company and its group organizations, and promoting improvements.

   2. Organization, personnel and procedures
        The internal auditing department conducts operational audits of business operation
        organizations and both management and operational audits of consolidated subsidiaries, in
        accordance with the Internal Audit Regulations and related internal rules. In principle, internal
        audits cover all business operating units and all consolidated subsidiaries. From among these
        organizations, each year, the General Manager of the Internal Auditing Department determines
        the audit targets using a risk-based approach that considers factors such as findings from
        previous audits and the time elapsed since the last audit. An audit plan is then formulated,
        identifying priority items to be verified for each audit target. This plan is reported in advance to
        the Audit Committee, approved by the Executive Committee, and subsequently reported to the
        Board of Directors before audits are conducted.
        Following each audit, the General Manager submits an internal audit report (a double report) to
        both the Representative Executive Officer & President and the Audit Committee, and sends a
        copy to the Executive Officer responsible for the audited organization and its general manager.
        Audited organizations are required to address the identified issues, and the internal auditing
        department follows up on the status of corrective actions. If there is any inconsistency between
        instructions from the Representative Executive Officer & President and those from the Audit
        Committee regarding an audit, the instructions of the Audit Committee take precedence.
        In addition to submitting the internal audit report, the department provides monthly updates and
        exchanges opinions with the Audit Committee members and the Representative Executive
        Officer & President. A report is also submitted to the Board of Directors and the Executive
        Committee semiannually.
        As of March 31, 2025, 25 personnel are involved in internal audits. These personnel bring
        diverse experience in areas such as domestic and international business, production, research,
        sales, finance and accounting, legal affairs, human resources, intellectual property, and IT. To
        enable them to contribute effectively to achieving management goals as audit professionals, the
        internal auditing department has defined a target auditor profile using a skill map and is
        working to continuously enhance their competencies through a structured training program
        based on that map. As part of these efforts, the Company encourages and supports employees in
        obtaining the Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) certification (as of the end of March 2025, six
        employees hold this qualification).
        The internal auditing department works closely with the internal auditing departments of both
        domestic and overseas consolidated subsidiaries to enhance audit quality across the Group.
        When the internal auditing departments of consolidated subsidiaries are assessed to have
        adequate systems and activities, the internal auditing department may rely on their audit results
        and omit all or part of its own procedures. Currently, the internal auditing department relies on
        audits of certain target organizations performed by the internal auditing departments of five
        domestic and four overseas subsidiaries (the “reliance parties”). Organizations audited by these
        reliance parties are not included in the internal auditing department’s audit plan; instead, each
        reliance party establishes its own audit plan in consultation with the Company’s internal

                                             - 139 -
    auditing department. The General Manager of the Internal Auditing Department also reports the
    results of audits conducted by the reliance parties to the Representative Executive Officer &
    President and the Audit Committee members. As of March 31, 2025, 16 personnel involved are
    involved in internal audits at domestic reliance parties and 25 at overseas reliance parties.
    The internal auditing department conducts self-assessments, and for reliance parties, the
    Department performs evaluations based on their respective self-assessments. The quality of
    internal audits conducted by both the internal auditing department and its reliance parties is
    evaluated annually. In addition, external evaluations are conducted once every five years to help
    ensure the effectiveness of audit activities.
    The Company’s internal auditing department also conducts evaluations and reports on internal
    control over financial reporting in accordance with the Financial Instruments and Exchange
    Act.

             In the event that the Accounting Auditor is recognized to have fallen under any of the items in
             Article 340, Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act, the Audit Committee shall dismiss the
             Accounting Auditor, based on the consent of all members of the Audit Committee. In this case,
             a member of the Audit Committee selected by the Audit Committee shall report the fact that
             the Accounting Auditor was dismissed and the reasons for the dismissal at the first General
             Meeting of Shareholders convened after the dismissal.
             In addition, if the Audit Committee recognizes that it is necessary to change the Accounting
             Auditor, such as cases when it conducts a comprehensive evaluation in accordance with
             evaluation indicators related to the Accounting Auditor’s qualifications, independence from
             the Company, expertise, and other criteria, and finds that there are issues preventing the
             Accounting Auditor from executing its duties, then it shall determine the content of a proposal
             related to the dismissal or non-reappointment of the Accounting Auditor to be submitted at the
             General Meeting of Shareholders.
             In accordance with the aforementioned policy, the Audit Committee conducted an evaluation
             of the audit firm’s performance and capabilities. For more information, please refer to the “(i)
             Status of audits by audit committee, 3. Main activities of Audit Committee members, 6)
             Evaluation of the Accounting Auditor and decisions on reappointment or non-reappointment.”

                                                       - 143 -
(4) Compensations for officers
     (i)    Matters regarding policies on determining the amount of compensations of officers and
            calculation method thereof
           1. Basic principles for officers’ compensations decisions
                Matters regarding policies on determining the amount of compensations of officers and
                calculation method thereof are decided by the Compensation Committee. The basic policy on
                determining officer compensation is as follows.
                1) In line with the Ajinomoto Group Policy (AGP), it will lead to medium- to long-term
                   expansion of the corporate value
                2) The level of compensations is sufficiently competitive with the market level
                3) Compensations will be determined through a transparent process that is accountable to
                   stakeholders

           2. Outline of compensations for officers

            1) Compensations of Executive Officers (including persons who concurrently serve as Directors)
                Comprised of the Basic Compensation, the Short-term Incentives (hereinafter referred to as
                “STI”), and the Medium-term Stock-based Incentives (hereinafter referred to as “MTI”), the
                details of which are as follow:
                i) Basic Compensation
                The Basic Compensation is a monetary compensation that is paid every month to fully
                demonstrate the qualities and abilities that drive corporate growth and to meet the
                responsibilities of employees. A fixed amount is paid monthly.
                ii) Short-term Incentives (STI)
                The STI is a monetary compensation that is paid at the end of June once a year, depending on
                the performance evaluation of the entire Company and each individual after the end of the
                fiscal year, as an incentive to encourage steady achievement of performance targets for a
                single fiscal year and appropriate management.
                iii) Medium-term Stock-based Incentives (MTI)
                The MTI is a performance-linked compensation that is assessed using a predetermined
                valuation index after the end of the three fiscal years commencing on April 1, 2023
                (hereinafter referred to as the “3-Year Period”) with the aim of achieving sustained medium-to
                long-term improvement in business performance and increasing corporate value of the
                Ajinomoto Group, and is paid in the Company’s shares and the amount equivalent to the
                conversion and disposal of the Company’s shares. The maximum amount of monies the
                Company contributes to the stock-granting trust (hereinafter referred to as the “Trust”) for the
                MTI is ¥2.2 billion for the 3-Year Period covered and the maximum amount of the
                Company’s shares to be acquired by the Trust in the money provided to the Trust is 1.1
                million. The number of the Company’s shares, etc. to be used for payment of MTI is obtained
                as follows. Each evaluation index (calculated from the target achievement rate and evaluation
                weight) is multiplied by the predetermined standard amount for each job position. Then, the
                total amount obtained (hereinafter referred to as the “amount of MTI”) is divided by the
                closing price (¥2,303.0) of the Company’s shares on March 31, 2023, to yield the number of
                shares to be used for payment of MTI. Half of the MTI will be delivered in the form of
                Company’s shares, and the remaining half will be delivered in cash to be used for payment of
                income tax, etc., therefore the Trust will convert this half to cash by selling the shares on the
                market and then paying the amount equivalent to the conversion and disposal of the
                Company’s shares. For Executive Officers who are non-Japan residents or Foreign Directors
                and Officers (as defined in 3. 2) ii) below), the MTI will be delivered in cash, using the
                currency specified in the “Standard amount by position.” However, Executive Officers and
                their successors who have been resolved by the Compensation Committee of the Company
                that they are not appropriate to receive the MTI in light of the purpose of such compensation
                system may not receive such compensation, and in the event a resolution is made by the
                Compensation Committee of the Company that it is not appropriate to pay the MTI to
                Executive Officers in light of the purpose of such compensation system, the Company may
                seek the return of such compensation from the person who received such compensation.

                                                  - 144 -
     The Company uses ROIC (return on invested capital after tax) and relative TSR (versus
     TOPIX) as economic value indicators, greenhouse gas emissions reduction rate and number of
     individuals whose healthy life expectancy has extended as social value indicators, and
     employee engagement score, percentage of global female managers, and corporate brand
     value as intangible asset enhancement indicators.

 2) Compensations for Independent Outside Directors and Internal Directors who are members of
    the Audit Committee
     The compensations for Independent Outside Directors shall be based solely on the Basic
     Compensation, which shall be paid monthly in a fixed amount of cash. The compensations for
     the Internal Directors who are members of the Audit Committee shall be based solely on the
     Basic Compensation, which shall be paid monthly in a fixed amount of cash.

3. Policy on determining the amount of compensation for individual officers

 1) How to determine compensations
     The amount of compensation will be determined by job position based on the responsibilities
     of supervision and execution performed by officers.

 2) How to determine levels of compensations
     i) Compensation levels for Internal Directors and Executive Officers are based on the 75th
     percentile (the top 25%) of that level (based on the results of surveys conducted by external
     organizations on about 20 companies that are similar in size to the Company and also have
     Nomination Committees in place).
     When such Internal Directors or Executive Officers concurrently serve as a president of an
     overseas group company of the Company, the Company will pay allowances due to overseas
     assignments and adjust the amount of compensations in consideration of the amount
     equivalent to individual income taxes that would be levied if the Internal Director or
     Executive Officer worked in Japan (reference: performance-linked compensation is calculated
     based on the income tax equivalent amount in accordance with the “Table of Withholding Tax
     Rates on Bonuses” issued by the National Tax Agency), and the amount of compensation
     from the overseas group company of the Company. If individual income taxes are incurred in
     the host country, the overseas group companies will bear the amount equivalent to such taxes.
     ii) Notwithstanding of the above, compensation levels for Internal Directors and Executive
     Officers who have the closest relationship with countries (or regions) other than Japan
     (“Foreign Directors and Officers”) are based on 50th to 75th percentiles (top 25% to 50%) of
     the level based on the results of surveys conducted by external organizations on companies
     that are similar in size and business type in the countries (or regions). (reference: As of the
     reporting date, Mr. Michael Lish is classified as an overseas officer, and the calculation of his
     performance-linked compensation is based on the U.S. standard amount by position.)
     The Company will adjust the amount of compensations from the Company in consideration of
     the amount of taxes that would be levied if they worked in that most closely related country or
     region. In addition to the above, if individual income taxes are incurred in Japan due to the
     appointment of a seconded person from an overseas group company to the Company as an
     Internal Director or Executive Officer, the Company will bear the amount equivalent to such
     taxes.
     iii) The level of compensations for Independent Outside Directors is based on the 75th
     percentile (the top 25%) of that level (based on the results of surveys conducted by external
     organizations on us and about 20 companies of Companies with Three Committees that are
     similar in size to the Company).

(v)         Performance index formula
          A performance evaluation index is calculated for each performance indicator based on
          the formulas presented in Table 1 and Table 2 below. However, for the performance
          indicators classified as “Social value indicators” and “Intangible asset enhancement
          indicators,” the achievement rate shall be 1.0 if the target is achieved and 0 if the target
          is not achieved. The maximum achievement rate of the performance evaluation index for
          the “Economic value indicator” is capped at 1.4. If the achievement rate falls below the
          non-payment standards defined in Table 2, the rate shall be deemed to be 0.6, regardless
          of the non-payment standards specified therein and the performance evaluation index for
          each indicator is then calculated accordingly.
          Notwithstanding the foregoing, the performance evaluation of an Executive Officer who
          falls under ii. (b) b) or (c) b) of “(i) The amount of Medium-term Stock-based Incentives
          (MTI)” shall be deemed to have achieved 100% of the target for each performance
          indicator. However, this exception shall not apply if the relevant event occurs between
          February 1 of the final fiscal year and the last day of the target period.

 Notes:
 1. ROIC (Return on Invested Capital) is calculated based on the following formula. All figures are
    consolidated amounts.
    ROIC (Return on Invested Capital) = (Operating profit after tax for the fiscal year) ÷ ((Invested capital for
    the fiscal year + Invested capital for the previous fiscal year) ÷ 2)
    Operating profit after tax = Operating profit x (1 - Income taxes ÷ Profit before income taxes)
    Invested capital = (Equity attributable to owners of the parent company) + (Interest-bearing debt)
    Interest-bearing debt = (Short-term borrowings) + (Commercial papers) + (Current portion of bonds) +
    (Current portion of long-term borrowings) + (Corporate bonds) + (Long-term borrowings) + (Short-term
    lease liabilities) + (Long-term lease liabilities)
 2. Relative TSR is calculated based on the following formula.
    Relative TSR = (Total Company shareholder return at the end of the latest fiscal year) ÷ (Total TOPIX
    shareholder return including dividends for the corresponding period used to calculate total Company
    shareholder return)
    Total Company shareholder return at the end of the latest fiscal year = (Share price at the end of the latest
    fiscal year + Cumulative amount of dividends per share of 4 fiscal years prior to the latest fiscal year
    through the latest fiscal year) ÷ Share price at the end of the fiscal year five years prior to the latest fiscal
    year
    Total TOPIX shareholder return including dividends for corresponding period used to calculate total
    Company shareholder return = TOPIX total returns including dividends at the end of the latest fiscal year
    ÷ TOPIX total returns including dividends at the end of the earliest previous fiscal year
 3. The Employee engagement score is evaluated by the average score of the 9 questions of the “ASV
    achievement process” and determined by achieved or not achieved.
 4. The Corporate brand value is evaluated by using the “Best Japan Brands” published by Interbrand.
 5. ROIC (Return on Invested Capital) achievement rate is calculated by the weighted total value of each
    fiscal year.
    Results for FY2023 ÷ Performance target for FY2023 x 25%
    Results for FY2024 ÷ Performance target for FY2024 x 25%
    Results for FY2025 ÷ Performance target for FY2025 x 50%

(5) Status of Shareholdings
     (i)   Criteria and approach for the classification of investment shares
           The Company classifies investment shares into those held for pure investment purposes and those
           held for other purposes. Investment shares held for pure investment purposes are those held solely
           to earn returns from fluctuations in share value or dividends. Investment shares held for purposes
           other than pure investment are classified as cross-shareholdings.

     (ii) Investment shares held for any purpose other than a pure investment purpose
          a. Holding policy and method of verifying the reasonableness of shareholding, and details of
          verification of appropriateness of holding of individual issues in the Board of Directors, etc.
             The Company does not, in principle, hold any cross-shareholdings, except for stocks for which
             we believe that transactions and alliances involving such holdings will contribute to enhancing
             the corporate value of the Ajinomoto Group (hereinafter referred to as “strategic holdings”).
             Whether a holding is to be deemed a strategic holding is determined comprehensively based on
             whether there are benefits associated with holding each individual stock (in terms of the
             qualitative effects of such holdings) or whether the Ajinomoto Group’s sales are commensurate
             with certain transaction requirements related to the WACC (weighted average cost of capital), as
             well as certain other quantitative factors.
             Every year, the Company reviews the propriety of holding shares through the Board of Directors
             and discloses the results of these reviews in its Corporate Governance Report.
             Those shares judged as inappropriate to hold as strategic holdings will be sold once the detailed
             plan for selling is determined. Additionally, even shares determined to be strategic holdings may
             be sold due to changes in external circumstances or other factors.
           b. Exercise of voting rights
             The Company will exercise voting rights of cross-shareholdings so as to contribute to improving
             long-term corporate value. The Company will vote against instances where shareholder value is
             significantly impaired due to organizational restructuring or other factors, or cases where serious
             concerns arise with regard to corporate governance for reasons such as social scandals.
           c. Cross-shareholders
             Should a company that holds shares of the Company as cross-shareholdings indicate their
             intentions to sell their shares, the Company will not suggest a reduction in the transaction nor
             otherwise interfere with the sale.
           d. Reduction of cross-shareholdings
             Since the introduction of the Corporate Governance Code, the Company has been working to
             reduce its cross-shareholdings.
             In FY2024, we sold a total of 20 stocks, comprising 6 unlisted shares and 14 stocks other than
             unlisted shares, for total proceeds of 13.5 billion yen. In addition, six unlisted stocks decreased
             due to liquidation and other factors.
             As a result of these efforts, the number and balance of cross-shareholdings have been steadily
             decreasing.

V.         Financial Information
1.   Basis of preparation of consolidated financial statements and non-consolidated financial statements
     (1)   The consolidated financial statements of the Company have been prepared in accordance with the International Accounting
           Standards (“IFRS”) pursuant to the provision of Article 312 of the “Regulation on Terminology, Forms, and Preparation
           Methods of Consolidated Financial Statements” (Ministry of Finance Order No. 28 of 1976).
     (2)   The non-consolidated financial statements of the Company have been prepared in accordance with the “Regulation on
           Terminology, Forms, and Preparation Methods of Financial Statements” (Ministry of Finance Order No. 59 of 1963; the
           “Regulation on Financial Statements”).
           In addition, the Company falls under the category of special companies submitting financial statements and has prepared
           the non-consolidated financial statements pursuant to Article 127 of the Regulation on Financial Statements.


2.   Note on independent audit
     The consolidated financial statements and the non-consolidated financial statements for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025
     (from April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025) were audited by KPMG AZSA LLC in accordance with the provision of Article 193-2,
     Paragraph 1 of the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act of Japan.


3.   Special efforts to ensure the appropriateness of the consolidated financial statements and notes and establishment of a system
     under which the consolidated financial statements and notes can be prepared in an appropriate manner under IFRS
     The Company has been making special efforts to ensure the appropriateness of the consolidated financial statements and notes
     and establishing a system under which the consolidated financial statements and notes can be prepared in an appropriate manner
     under IFRS. The details are as follows:
     (1) In order to develop a system that can respond appropriately to changes in accounting standards, the Company employs
           people with knowledge of IFRS accounting standards and joins the organization of Financial Accounting Standards
           Foundation and participates in its training programs to accumulate specialized knowledge.
     (2)   In order to prepare appropriate consolidated financial statements in accordance with IFRS accounting standards, the
           Company has prepared the Ajinomoto Group Accounting Policies in accordance with IFRS accounting standards, and
           conducts accounting procedures based on the policies. The Company obtains press releases and standards issued by the
           International Accounting Standards Board and updates the content of the Ajinomoto Group Accounting Policies after
           examining the latest standards and their impact on the Company.
